title: Compatible dimension shifting for sheaf systems on a spectral inverse limit.
statement: Let I be a nonempty directed preorder, S_i spectral spaces and f_ij : S_j → S_i spectral maps with identity and composition laws [def-weil-spectral-space]. Let the spectral space X with compatible projections p_i be their topological inverse limit, both on points and with the initial topology. Let F_i be abelian sheaves on S_i with f-maps alpha_ij satisfying the sectionwise identity and composition laws [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. Let P : I → Ab(X) be a diagram with colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with isomorphisms eP_i : P_i ≅ p_i⁻¹F_i, whose transitions on unit sections are the specified alpha_ij. Then there is a compatible system R_i with maps rho_ij satisfying the same sectionwise laws, and a diagram Q : I → Ab(X) with colimit and isomorphisms eQ_i : Q_i ≅ p_i⁻¹R_i whose transitions agree with rho_ij on unit sections. There are maps d_i,n : H^n(S_i,R_i) → H^(n+1)(S_i,F_i) and D_n : H^n(X,colim Q) → H^(n+1)(X,colim P) [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], with each D_n surjective. For every index i, degree n, normalized pullback family c_i [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback-data], and class x in H^n(S_i,R_i), the canonical maps [def-weil-pbc-spectral-limit-cohomology-map] from the coprojections satisfy b_i,F,n+1(d_i,n(x)) = D_n(b_i,R,n(x)). These are the connecting maps of the compatible injective embeddings and quotient sequences from Tag 0A37. No representation or eventual detection of cohomology classes is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0A37, lemma-colimit, compatible injective construction and final Cech vanishing paragraph

proof.text: The spectral inverse-limit theorem gives spectral projections, so each $p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ is quasi-compact when $U_i$ is. The limit topology has a basis of finite intersections of inverse images of opens. Refine each stage open by its quasi-compact-open basis. For finitely many resulting opens choose a common upper index $k$; their intersection is $p_k^{-1}(\bigcap_l f_{i_lk}^{-1}U_{i_l})$, whose stage open is quasi-compact by spectrality and quasi-separatedness. Thus these inverse images form a basis. The descent-opens lemma represents every quasi-compact open at a stage and detects inclusions and finite covering equalities at later stages, as needed below.

source.place: Tag 0A30, label lemma-descend-opens; Tag 0A2Z, spectral inverse-limit basis

proof.text: Apply the section comparison to the compatible sheaf system on X. It identifies sections of F over p_i^{-1}(U_i) with the filtered colimit of the sections of F_j over f_{ij}^{-1}(U_i), and the comparison is the canonical one induced by the transition maps.

Use the full site of open subsets of each X_i with arbitrary open coverings, not a finite-cover colimit site. Its objects and inclusion morphisms form sets; unions of open covers and intersections verify the site axioms. Choose embeddings e_k:F_k\to A_k with A_k injective using enough injectives on this site. Define G_i(V)=\prod_{k\ge i}A_k(f_{ik}^{-1}V), with componentwise restrictions. This is a sheaf: a compatible local family glues uniquely in each factor, and those gluings give the unique product section. It is the product of the sheaves (f_{ik})_*A_k, with its universal property verified componentwise. Each factor is injective by the topological pushforward-injective lemma, which assumes only continuity; the product-injectives lemma gives injectivity of G_i.

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, compatible injective construction and dimension shifting

proof.text: Define \gamma_i:F_i\to G_i by its k-component (f_{ik})_*e_k\circ\alpha_{ik}. Its i-component is e_i because \alpha_{ii}=1, so \gamma_i is monic. Define \beta_{ij}:G_i\to(f_{ij})_*G_j on an open V by discarding coordinates k not \ge j; the retained k-coordinate lies in A_k(f_{jk}^{-1}f_{ij}^{-1}V)=A_k(f_{ik}^{-1}V). Thus \beta_{ii}=1, and both \beta_{ik} and (f_{ij})_*\beta_{jk}\circ\beta_{ij} retain exactly the coordinates l\ge k. On coordinate k\ge j, (f_{ij})_*\gamma_j\circ\alpha_{ij} equals (f_{ik})_*e_k\circ(f_{ij})_*\alpha_{jk}\circ\alpha_{ij}=(f_{ik})_*e_k\circ\alpha_{ik}, the same as \beta_{ij}\circ\gamma_i. These are sheaf maps since coordinate projections commute with restrictions. Take adjoints to obtain the required compatible inverse-image system of injectives. This proves the construction here rather than applying the finite-cover-site system lemma.

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, compatible injective construction and dimension shifting

proof.text: Let Q_i=\operatorname{coker}(\gamma_i). Inverse image along every continuous f_{ij} and p_i is exact: the sheafPullback construction is left adjoint, hence preserves cokernels, and its finite-limit preservation (Mathlib sheafPullbackConstruction.preservesFiniteLimits, using flatness of Opens.map) preserves kernels. This is the exactness used in the proof of the cited pushforward-injective lemma. The compatible maps from the preceding step therefore induce maps f_{ij}^{-1}Q_i\to Q_j by the cokernel universal property; their identity and composition laws follow by precomposing the epimorphisms f_{ij}^{-1}G_i\to f_{ij}^{-1}Q_i. Pulling back 0\to F_i\to G_i\to Q_i\to0 along p_i remains exact. Applying exact filtered colimits on the full open-set site of X gives 0\to F\to G\to Q\to0, where G=\varinjlim_i p_i^{-1}G_i and Q=\varinjlim_i p_i^{-1}Q_i. No finite-cover hypothesis is used in either cited exactness statement.

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, compatible injective construction and dimension shifting

proof.text: Let B be the quasi-compact opens of X and Cov all finite coverings of members of B by members of B. They are cofinal among arbitrary open coverings: refine each covering by the quasi-compact-open basis and extract a finite subcover using quasi-compactness of the target. Finite intersections remain in B by spectrality. Descend a finite covering U=\bigcup_l U_l and its members to one stage using the open-descent lemma; the finite-stage equality is eventually a covering equality. For every later stage the pulled-back covering is still a covering and its finite intersections are quasi-compact since the transition maps are spectral. Step 2 applied to the G_i identifies each term of the ordered Cech complex with its filtered-colimit counterpart. In each fixed degree there are only finitely many tuples: a tuple of finitely many colimit sections is represented at a common stage, and equality is also detected at a common stage, so finite products commute with this colimit. Restrictions are the same under these identifications, hence so are the alternating differentials. The finite-stage complexes have zero positive cohomology by the topological injective-Cech lemma, and exact filtered colimits of abelian groups preserve this exactness. The site Cech-vanishing criterion now applies on the full open-set site, with B and Cov as above, and gives H^p(U,G)=0 for every U in B and p>0, in particular for U=X.

source.place: Tag 0A37, lemma-colimit, final proof paragraph using Tags 0A30, 01EP and 01EW

proof.text: The compatible embeddings and cokernel projections give natural transformations between the pulled-back coefficient diagrams. Their colimit short exact sequence has first object colim P and third object colim Q. At each index the inverse-image sequence maps into this colimit sequence by the coprojections. Its first and third components are precisely eP_i inverse followed by the P coprojection and eQ_i inverse followed by the Q coprojection. The stage maps form a short-complex morphism by the defining squares for the diagram maps and colimit coprojections. Apply normalized pullback compatibility with Yoneda boundaries to the stage exact sequence and then extension-class naturality to this short-complex morphism. Restriction along the equality p_i inverse-image(top)=top commutes with the boundary by equality induction. Their composition is the canonical boundary identity asserted in the conclusion. Define d_i,n and D_n to be these Yoneda boundaries. Since the middle limit sheaf has zero cohomology in degree n+1, the covariant Ext exact sequence implies that D_n is surjective: every class maps to zero in that middle group. This is a dimension-shifting construction, with no induction or finite-stage class representation.

theorem spectralLimit_acyclic_replacement
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (S : I → TopCat.{u}) [∀ i : I, SpectralSpace (S i)]
    (f : ∀ (i j : I), i ≤ j → (S j ⟶ S i))
    (hf : ∀ (i j : I) (h : i ≤ j), IsSpectralMap (f i j h))
    (hfid : ∀ i : I, f i i le_rfl = 𝟙 (S i))
    (hfcomp : ∀ (i j k : I) (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k),
      f j k hjk ≫ f i j hij = f i k (hij.trans hjk))
    (X : TopCat.{u}) [SpectralSpace X] (p : ∀ i : I, X ⟶ S i)
    (hpcomp : ∀ (i j : I) (h : i ≤ j), p j ≫ f i j h = p i)
    (hlimit : ∀ a : ∀ i : I, S i,
      (∀ (i j : I) (h : i ≤ j), f i j h (a j) = a i) →
      ∃! x : X, ∀ i : I, p i x = a i)
    (htop : X.str = ⨅ i : I, TopologicalSpace.induced (p i) (S i).str)
    (F : ∀ i : I, (S i).Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (α : ∀ (i j : I) (h : i ≤ j),
      F i ⟶ (pushforward AddCommGrpCat.{u} (f i j h)).obj (F j))
    (hαid : ∀ (i : I) (U : Opens (S i)) (s : (F i).obj.obj (op U)),
      HEq ((α i i le_rfl).hom.app (op U) s) s)
    (hαcomp : ∀ (i j k : I) (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k)
      (U : Opens (S i)) (s : (F i).obj.obj (op U)),
      HEq ((α i k (hij.trans hjk)).hom.app (op U) s)
        ((α j k hjk).hom.app (op ((Opens.map (f i j hij)).obj U))
          ((α i j hij).hom.app (op U) s)))
    (P : I ⥤ X.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u}) [HasColimit P]
    (eP : ∀ i : I, P.obj i ≅
      (sheafPullback (Opens.map (p i)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology (S i)) (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)).obj (F i))
    (hP : ∀ (i j : I) (h : i ≤ j) (U : Opens (S i)) (s : (F i).obj.obj (op U)),
      HEq (((eP i).inv ≫ P.map (homOfLE h) ≫ (eP j).hom).hom.app
          (op ((Opens.map (p i)).obj U))
        (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Opens.map (p i)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology (S i)) (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)).unit.app
            (F i)).hom.app (op U) s))
        (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Opens.map (p j)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology (S j)) (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)).unit.app
            (F j)).hom.app (op ((Opens.map (f i j h)).obj U))
              ((α i j h).hom.app (op U) s)))
 :
    ∃ (R : ∀ i : I, (S i).Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u})
      (ρ : ∀ (i j : I) (h : i ≤ j),
        R i ⟶ (pushforward AddCommGrpCat.{u} (f i j h)).obj (R j))
      (hρid : ∀ (i : I) (U : Opens (S i)) (s : (R i).obj.obj (op U)),
        HEq ((ρ i i le_rfl).hom.app (op U) s) s)
      (hρcomp : ∀ (i j k : I) (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k)
        (U : Opens (S i)) (s : (R i).obj.obj (op U)),
        HEq ((ρ i k (hij.trans hjk)).hom.app (op U) s)
          ((ρ j k hjk).hom.app (op ((Opens.map (f i j hij)).obj U))
            ((ρ i j hij).hom.app (op U) s)))
      (Q : I ⥤ X.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (_ : HasColimit Q)
      (eQ : ∀ i : I, Q.obj i ≅
        (sheafPullback (Opens.map (p i)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology (S i)) (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)).obj (R i))
      (hQ : ∀ (i j : I) (h : i ≤ j) (U : Opens (S i)) (s : (R i).obj.obj (op U)),
        HEq (((eQ i).inv ≫ Q.map (homOfLE h) ≫ (eQ j).hom).hom.app
            (op ((Opens.map (p i)).obj U))
          (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Opens.map (p i)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
            (Opens.grothendieckTopology (S i)) (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)).unit.app
              (R i)).hom.app (op U) s))
          (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Opens.map (p j)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
            (Opens.grothendieckTopology (S j)) (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)).unit.app
              (R j)).hom.app (op ((Opens.map (f i j h)).obj U))
                ((ρ i j h).hom.app (op U) s)))
      (d : ∀ (i : I) (n : ℕ),
        CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H' (R i) n ⊤ → CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H' (F i) (n + 1) ⊤)
      (D : ∀ n : ℕ, CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H' (colimit Q) n ⊤ →
        CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H' (colimit P) (n + 1) ⊤),
      (∀ n : ℕ, Function.Surjective (D n)) ∧
      ∀ (i : I)
        (c : SiteCohomologyFamily (Opens.grothendieckTopology (S i))
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (Opens.map (p i)))
        (_ : @SiteCohomologyFamily.IsPullback _ _ _ _
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology (S i)) (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
          (Opens.map (p i)) inferInstance
          (@Adjunction.left_adjoint_additive _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _
            (sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Opens.map (p i)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
              (Opens.grothendieckTopology (S i)) (Opens.grothendieckTopology X))
            (Functor.additive_of_preserves_binary_products _))
          inferInstance inferInstance c)
        (n : ℕ) (x : CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H' (R i) n ⊤),
        (spectralLimitCohomologyMap (p i) c
          ((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Opens.map (p i)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
            (Opens.grothendieckTopology (S i)) (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)).homEquiv
              (F i) (colimit P) ((eP i).inv ≫ colimit.ι P i)) (n + 1)).hom (d i n x) =
        D n ((spectralLimitCohomologyMap (p i) c
          ((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Opens.map (p i)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
            (Opens.grothendieckTopology (S i)) (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)).homEquiv
              (R i) (colimit Q) ((eQ i).inv ≫ colimit.ι Q i)) n).hom x)
